title: Revelation
definition: Revelation is God making Himself known to humanity. God reveals His character, will, works, and redemptive purpose so that people may know Him, trust Him, worship Him, and walk with Him.
summary: Scripture teaches that God has not left humanity in darkness. He has revealed Himself generally through creation and providence, and specially through His Word, His prophets, and supremely through Jesus Christ. All true doctrine begins with God taking the initiative to make Himself known. The goal of revelation is not information alone, but communion with God through Christ and obedience by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: General Revelation
studySections.content: General revelation refers to God making aspects of Himself known through creation, conscience, and His providential care over the world. The heavens declare the glory of God, and creation testifies to His power and divine nature. General revelation is real, but because of sin, humanity suppresses the truth and needs the light of God’s saving revelation in Christ.

studySections.heading: Special Revelation
studySections.content: Special revelation is God making Himself known in saving truth through His spoken Word, His written Word, and ultimately through His Son, Jesus Christ. Hebrews 1:1-2 teaches that God spoke in many ways through the prophets, but has now spoken in His Son. This makes Christ the fullness and center of God’s revelation.

studySections.heading: Revelation and the Holy Spirit
studySections.content: The Holy Spirit opens the heart and mind to receive the truth God has revealed. Spiritual truth is not merely discovered by human reasoning; it must be received by faith as the Spirit bears witness to the Word and leads believers into the truth of Christ.
